title: 第13章 签到变异陷死局第14章 残片异动惹纷争
slug: 签到玄天我成了万界守护者
content_zh:
方浩踩着玄龟留下的湿漉漉爪印往前走，鞋底黏着几片灰烬，像是从谁家烧塌的祠堂里顺脚蹭来的。
他没理那石碑上“少主说”
的狗屁建议，倒是一路琢磨那行小字到底是不是黑猫爪子刻的——毕竟那家伙连磨爪子都懒得自己动手。
可刚翻过山脊，左手腕忽然一沉，像被人往血脉里灌了半斤铁砂。
他低头一看，掌心那条河状纹路正一跳一跳地往指尖爬，颜色也由淡灰转成乌青。
“这玩意儿是签到送的还是附赠的？”
他嘀咕着，顺手从袖兜摸出一块烤灵鼠的油纸，咬了一口才发现是冷的。
油没热，人先热了。
一股阴风从脊椎底下往上窜，不是冷，也不是疼，倒像是有人拿根锈铁丝在他骨头缝里慢慢搅。
他眯眼望向前方，断魂原的边界就在三里外，焦土如龟裂的锅底，连风刮过去都带着股焦糊味。
他本不想去。
但识海里的星尘这几天总在半夜自己打转，绕着那条河纹转圈，转得他睡不踏实。
昨夜还梦见自己站在一口井边，井里浮着九张脸，全闭着眼，嘴角却咧到耳根。
梦不算吓人，吓人的是他醒来时，发现枕头底下压着一张符——不是他贴的，也不是系统给的，上面画了把剑，剑尖朝下，底下写着个“九”
他把符烧了，灰烬飘到窗台，拼成了半个“血”
字。
现在，那股搅动骨头的劲儿越来越急，像是在催他。
“去就去。”
他把油纸团成球，塞进嘴里嚼了两下吐掉，“反正最近也没抽到厕纸券。”
他蹽着步子进了断魂原，逐流步法贴着地皮滑行，专挑那些裂缝窄的地方跳。

怨灵残影在远处游荡，三五成群，像赶集的散修，看见活人也不扑，只歪着头盯，眼眶里飘着绿火。
方浩路过一具半埋的骸骨，顺手签到。
【签到地点：断魂原边缘】
【奖励：腐土馒头x1】
他看了一眼那团黑乎乎的东西，塞进怀里。
“留着喂黑猫，看它还敢不敢拿猫薄荷坑人。”
再往里走，空气开始发涩，呼吸像在舔铁锈。
星图法衣自动亮起，微光绕着肩头转了两圈，像是在提醒他：再往前，别怪我不保。
“我知道，我知道。”
他拍了拍衣领，“你比我还怕死。”
content_en:
Fang Hao stepped forward on the wet paw prints left by the black turtle. There were a few pieces of ashes stuck to the soles of his shoes, as if they had come from someone's burned down ancestral hall.
He ignored the "Young Master said" on the stone tablet
The bullshit suggestion was that he was wondering whether the small words were carved by the black cat's claws - after all, the guy didn't even bother to sharpen his claws himself.
But just after crossing the ridge, my left wrist suddenly sank, as if someone poured half a kilogram of iron sand into my blood.
He lowered his head and saw that the river-shaped lines on his palm were jumping towards his fingertips, and the color also changed from light gray to dark green.
"Is this a gift for signing in or is it a bonus?"
He muttered, and took out a piece of oil paper for roasting the rat from his sleeve pocket. He took a bite and realized that it was cold.
The oil is not hot, the people are hot first.
A cold wind rushed up from the bottom of his spine. It wasn't cold or painful, but it felt like someone was slowly stirring a rusty wire between his bones.
He squinted and looked ahead. The boundary of Duanhunyuan was just three miles away. The scorched earth was like the cracked bottom of a pot, and even the wind carried a burning smell.
He didn't want to go.
But the stardust in the sea of ​​consciousness kept spinning around in the middle of the night these past few days, circling around the river pattern, making it difficult for him to sleep well.
Last night, I dreamed that I was standing by a well, and there were nine faces floating in the well, all with their eyes closed, but the corners of their mouths were grinning from ear to ear.
The dream was not scary. What was scary was that when he woke up, he found a talisman under his pillow - it was not posted by him, nor was it given by the system. It had a sword drawn on it, with the tip of the sword pointing down, and "Nine" written underneath.
He burned the talisman, and the ashes floated to the window sill, forming half of "blood"
words.
Now, the force that stirs the bones is getting faster and faster, as if urging him.
"Just go."
He balled the oil paper into a ball, stuffed it into his mouth, chewed it twice and spit it out, "I haven't gotten any toilet paper coupons recently anyway."
He stepped into the Broken Soul Plain, gliding along the ground with his step-by-step footwork, specializing in the narrow cracks to jump.
The afterimages of the resentful spirits wandered in the distance, in small groups, like casual cultivators going to the market. They did not pounce when they saw a living person, they only stared at them with their heads tilted, with green fire floating in their eye sockets.
Fang Hao passed by a half-buried skeleton and signed in.
[Sign-in location: Edge of Duanhunyuan]
[Reward: Futu Steamed Bun x1]
He glanced at the dark thing and stuffed it into his arms.
"Keep it and feed it to the black cat to see if it dares to trick people with catnip."
Walking further inside, the air begins to feel astringent, and breathing feels like licking rust.
The Star Chart Vestment automatically lit up, and the dim light circled twice around his shoulders, as if to remind him: If you go forward, don't blame me for not being able to protect you.
"I know, I know."
He patted his collar and said, "You are more afraid of death than me."
